object.Title: Kneeling King
object.Description:
The king kneels with his torso inclined forward and his arms reaching to hold something that is now missing. He wears a striped royal head-cloth and uraeus. He wears a pleated kilt and a collar. Beneath his knees and feet are prongs for insertion into a base.

For the latest information about this object, Kneeling King, visit the Online Collection of the Walters Art Museum.
object.Provenance: Dikran Kelekian, Paris and New York [date and mode of acquisition unknown] [said to have been found at the pyramids]; Henry Walters, Baltimore, 1911, by purchase; Walters Art Museum, 1931, by bequest.
object.MuseumLocation: To learn whether this object is now on view, and in which gallery, visit https://purl.thewalters.org/art/54.2103
